texts: For recurrent pericarditis after aspirin and ibuprofen have failed, the treatment is colchicine added to a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug such as ibuprofen.
Colchicine halves the risk of further recurrences and is given for several months, with the NSAID tapered once the symptoms settle.
Corticosteroids act quickly but make recurrences more likely, so they are kept for patients who cannot take, or do not respond to, NSAIDs and colchicine.
Azathioprine and intrapericardial treatment are later options for resistant cases.
In the picture, the cold chicken with its crocus and the owl professor cool the hot red dress, while the stereo stays on the shelf.
Memory hook: the chicken and the owl stop the boomerang; the stereo brings it back.
